# C-2 · Security Categorization

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Step | C Categorize (system level) |
| Phases | PH-MSA (primary), PH-TMRR |
| Depends on | C-1, P-12 |
| Inputs | ART-SD, ART-BIA, ART-INFOTYPES, ART-RA, EXT-CNSSI1253-OVERLAYS |
| Outputs | ART-CAT (produces), ART-BIA (updates) |
| Writes facts | categorization |
| Minimum interviews | 1 |
| RACI | R: PER-ISSM, PER-IO · A: PER-PM · C: PER-UR, PER-ISSE, PER-PRIV, PER-CISO, PER-RE · I: PER-AO · PER-PRIV only when the system processes PII |
| Persona cards | [PER-ISSM](../../personas/PER-ISSM.md), [PER-IO](../../personas/PER-IO.md), [PER-PM](../../personas/PER-PM.md), [PER-UR](../../personas/PER-UR.md), [PER-ISSE](../../personas/PER-ISSE.md), [PER-PRIV](../../personas/PER-PRIV.md), [PER-CISO](../../personas/PER-CISO.md), [PER-RE](../../personas/PER-RE.md) |

Purpose: Categorize the system per CNSSI 1253, an impact level for each information type and the high-water mark for each security objective (C/I/A) plus the applicable overlays, and record it in facts.yaml.
<!-- END rmf:header -->
<!-- rmf:body authored -->

## Steps

1. **Entry check.** `uv run rmf status <run>` names C-2; C-1 is done and
   `artifacts/data/infotypes.yaml` exists (from P-12, or seeded). Why: the categorization is
   derived from the information types, and the system description says what the system
   does with them.
2. **Read the inputs** in `## Inputs`, and the CNSSI 1253 procedure:
   `uv run rmf refs show CNSSI1253 --section "3.1.1"` and
   `uv run rmf refs show CNSSI1253 --section "3.1.2"`.
3. **Interview** each information owner, then PER-ISSM (`## Interviews`).
   - Each information owner sets the impact level of the types they own (CNSSI 1253 §3.1).
     ART-INFOTYPES names the owner of each type: interview PER-IO for information owned
     outside the program, and PER-PM for information the program itself owns. Ask each to
     confirm or adjust every provisional C, I and A value of their types in
     `infotypes.yaml`, and to give the reason for any adjustment.
   - The ISSM confirms the overlay applicability and the system-level result.
4. **Settle the value per information type and objective.** For each `INF-*` record and
   each of C, I, A, the value is the IO's answer; absent an adjustment, it is `selected`
   when present, otherwise `base`. Record every adjustment with its reason and answer token.
   Do not edit `infotypes.yaml`: P-12 owns it, and C-2 does not list ART-INFOTYPES as an
   output.
5. **Compute the system categorization.** For each objective, take the highest value over
   all information types (the high-water mark, CNSSI 1253 §3.1.2 step 1). Never lower a
   value to reduce the number of controls; tailoring (S-2) handles that. Why: CNSSI 1253
   forbids changing the categorization to reflect management decisions about control
   stringency. Review the provisional levels against the organization, environment,
   mission, use and data sharing (SP 800-60 Step 3), within the overall national interest
   (FIPS 199), and record them in `factors_reviewed`. A system-level factor (aggregation,
   critical functionality, time criticality, public visibility, reliant systems,
   replacement cost, legal or statutory reasons, PII, critical infrastructure) may raise an
   objective above the mark: record each raise under `adjustments` with `from`, `to`,
   `factor` and `rationale`. A system is never below the mark (CATG-001). CUI and CTI hold
   confidentiality at no less than moderate (DoDI 8500.01), software artifacts with a
   military or space application confidentiality and integrity at moderate (DoWI 8430.01),
   and no information type may be classified above the system's classification (CATG-002).
   Record in `revisit` when the categorization is revisited: at significant or situational
   change, and at least every three years (SP 800-60).
6. **Determine the overlays.** Check each CNSSI 1253 overlay the run's references hold
   against the system:
   - Privacy Overlays (`CNSSI1253F-ATT6-PRIVACY`): applies when the system processes PII.
     Pick its control sets with the overlay's two questions (§4.1, `uv run rmf refs show
     CNSSI1253F-ATT6-PRIVACY --page 12 --anchor "Question 1"`) and record each set's ID,
     never the bare reference ID:
     - PII other than audit logs and account records: one of
       `CNSSI1253F-ATT6-PRIVACY-LOW`, `-MODERATE` or `-HIGH`, from the privacy risk level.
       The overlay's privacy risk analysis replaces the PCIL: record in ART-CAT
       `## Overlays` each of the seven Appendix factors with the risk level you selected for
       it (none may be dropped), any factor added for an exceptional case and why, how the
       factors were weighed into the overall privacy risk level, and the SAOP's (PER-PRIV)
       approval of that level. All PII counts: the overlay has no business contact exception.
     - Audit logs or account management records (almost every system with users):
       `CNSSI1253F-ATT6-PRIVACY-ACCT`. A system whose only PII is in those records gets
       the ACCT set alone.
   - Classified information overlay (`CNSSI1253E-ATT5-CLASSIFIED`): applies when it
     processes classified information.
   - Space platform overlay (`CNSSI1253F-ATT2-SPACE`): applies to space systems.
   - Any overlay `artifacts/ART-ORG-CONTEXT.md` mandates.

   Record the applicable overlays by ID, or an empty list, with a reason for each overlay
   you rule out. FACTS-001 rejects an ID `rmf baseline resolve` cannot apply (for example
   the bare Privacy Overlay ID, or the untranscribed Space Platform Overlay); its message
   lists the IDs to use.
7. **Write the categorization fact.** Rewrite `facts.yaml` whole, keeping every existing
   field, and set:

   ```yaml
   categorization:
     c: moderate
     i: moderate
     a: low
     overlays: []
     method: cnssi1253
     factors_reviewed: [organization, environment, mission, use, data-sharing, national-interest]
     adjustments: []  # {objective, from, to, factor, rationale} per raised objective
     set_by_task: C-2
     sources: [INT-006.A1, INT-006.A2, INT-007.A1, ART-INFOTYPES]
   ```

   - Values are `low`, `moderate` or `high`. `method` is `cnssi1253`. Only if the CNSSI1253
     entry in `references/index.yaml` has `status: degraded`, use `high-water-mark`, add
     assumption `ASM-BASELINE-001` ("categorized by the FIPS 199 high-water mark with
     SP 800-60 because CNSSI 1253 is unavailable"), and say so in ART-CAT.
   - Do **not** write `approved`; C-3 does. Why: S-1 refuses an unapproved categorization,
     and the approval must come from the AO or AODR (FACTS-001).
8. **Write `artifacts/ART-CAT.md`** from `templates/artifacts/ART-CAT.md`:
   - an impact table per information type and objective, with the basis for each value
     (`[[INT-###.A#]]`, or `[[ART-INFOTYPES]]` where the provisional value was kept);
   - how the system values follow from the table (the high-water mark per objective);
   - the overlay determination, one line per overlay considered.
   - Do not restate the system's trigraph or the overlay list as values in prose; the facts
     block that `rmf build` injects shows them (INV-4). Refer to it ("the system
     categorization in the facts block").
9. **Build and check.** `uv run rmf build <run>`, then `uv run rmf check <run> --task C-2`,
   until 0 errors.
10. **Journal** a CHECKPOINT.

## Interviews

| Persona | Why | Question focus |
|---|---|---|
| PER-IO | responsible (R); CNSSI 1253 makes each information owner set the impact of their information | for each information type: confirm or adjust C, I, A; consequences of disclosure, tampering and loss; whether any type is PII or classified |
| PER-ISSM | responsible (R) | the overlays that apply, information types missing from the list, consistency with the risk assessment |
| PER-PM (when the program owns information types) | accountable (A); owner of program information | the same questions as PER-IO, for the program's own types |
| PER-ISSE (optional) | consulted (C) | whether the architecture adds information (keys, configurations) not yet typed |

At least 1 interview; this playbook expects the PER-IO and PER-ISSM interviews. When the
system has several information owners, interview each (CNSSI 1253 §3.1: all information
owners provide input).

## Inputs

- `artifacts/ART-SD.md`
- `artifacts/ART-INFOTYPES.md`, `artifacts/data/infotypes.yaml`
- `artifacts/ART-RA.md`
- `product/profile.yaml` (proposed categorization and overlays: proposals only)
- References: CNSSI1253 §3.1, §3.1.1, §3.1.2; FIPS 199 page 10; the overlay attachments
  named in step 6

## Outputs

| File | Front-matter | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `artifacts/ART-CAT.md` | `artifact_id: ART-CAT`, `produced_by_task: C-2`, `touched_by: [C-2]` | C-3 appends itself |
| `facts.yaml` | — | `categorization` (without `approved`) |

## Facts

| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `categorization.c`, `.i`, `.a` | high-water mark per objective over all information types | the IO's answers and ART-INFOTYPES |
| `categorization.overlays` | applicable overlay reference IDs, or `[]` | the ISSM's answer |
| `categorization.method` | `cnssi1253` | — |

## Done when

- `facts.yaml` has `categorization` with `c`, `i`, `a`, `overlays` and `set_by_task: C-2`,
  and no `approved` field written by C-2.
- ART-CAT records the impact per information type and security objective, the basis for each
  value, and the overlay determination.
- `uv run rmf check <run> --task C-2` reports 0 errors.

## Journal and lessons

- CHECKPOINT: `## <time> · CHECKPOINT · task C-2`, with the number of information types and
  adjustments.
- If the result differs from `product/profile.yaml`'s proposal, say so in the CHECKPOINT body
  and why.
- RETRY and lesson rules: `_shared/journaling-and-lessons.md`.
